name: risor-generalized-object-keyed-collections
instr:
Risor cannot currently use Objects as equality-consistent map keys and set members. Support both runtime APIs and compiled scripts without string conversion. Accept stable values and identity-based objects, but reject mutable values whose equality changes.

Equal hashable Objects must share hash identities. Unhashable Objects must raise typed HashError before mutation. Follow existing Equals semantics for Boolean, Byte, Cell, Closure, Builtin, Color, Regexp, and external Object implementations, keeping hashes stable across permitted mutation. Resolve collisions with Object.Equals.

Generalized maps must retain original Object keys during insertion, replacement, lookup, containment, deletion, copying, updating, and equality. Map.SetObject, Map.GetObject, Map.DeleteObject, and Map.Entries expose this behavior. Set must provide equality-based deduplication, membership, removal, length, truthiness, enumeration, inspection, and equality through Set.Add, Set.Remove, Set.Has, and Set.Items. Both collections use first-insertion order. Replacement keeps position; reinsertion after deletion appends. Set union, intersection, and difference do not mutate operands.

Compiled key expressions, map spread, indexing, assignment, and deletion must preserve these rules. Failures must be atomic, catchable Risor errors without panics. Preserve NewMap string-key helpers, attributes, ownership, native conversion, JSON output, bare-identifier map keys, Eval options, scalar results, and ordinary eval
